append.text: **Ps 38:2 *Custódiam vias meas* → *Guardarei os meus caminhos*; 38:2b the noun *Pósui ori meo custódiam* → *Pus guarda à minha boca*** — the Latin's (and Greek's) echo kept by verb and noun of one root. The blind reader heard 'be careful how I live' first. **140:3 *Pone, Dómine, custódiam ori meo* should copy the noun.**

**Ps 38:3 *sílui a bonis* → *fiquei em silêncio quanto às coisas boas*** (draft 1 *sobre coisas boas*: topic, refused by the Latinist and the stylist; draft 2 *longe do bem*: spatial, refused at the gate; *quanto às* is the gate's fix and keeps both readings — withheld even good things / silent about them). Both readers asked for *calar-se* — refused, tacére's verb, and 38:13b *Ne síleas* → *Não fiqueis em silêncio* (= 34:22) is the same Latin verb.

Ps 38:4 *exardéscet ignis* → *um fogo se inflamará* (the Latin's future, passed the Latinist twice). concaléscere beside it → *arder* (*O meu coração ardeu dentro de mim*): draft 1 *se aqueceu* was heard by the blind reader as 'comforted'.

**Ps 38:6b, 38:7, 38:12b — three times in one psalm, *Todavia* each time** (the row; the stylist: 'the three todavia give it a sober spine'). The Greek is πλήν / μέντοιγε, often asseverative (DRB 'indeed … surely'); the blind reader heard 'an unclear contrast' at 38:6b. *Na verdade* is option 2 of Ps 38's `verumtamen`. Passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 38:8 *quæ est exspectátio mea? Nonne Dóminus?* → *qual é a minha espera? Não é o Senhor?*** — draft 1 had the row's clause (*que é que eu aguardo?*); the Latinist (minor) and the stylist ('filler') both asked for the noun *espera*; taken. **Proposal for the row: *espera* is the plain noun it lacked (waiting, not hope) where exspectátio stands as subject or predicate; *pelo que aguardo* stays for 118:116's *ab exspectatióne*. Cost: *espera* shares the root of *esperar* (D36's cost).** Greek here ὑπομονή.

Ps 38:8 *substántia mea apud te est* → *o meu ser está junto de vós* (Greek παρὰ σοῦ, 'from you' — the Latin followed); 38:13b *ádvena ego sum apud te* → *forasteiro junto de vós*. Passed the Latinist twice; the blind reader heard 'I am close to you' and 'a stranger living with you'.
Ps 38:9 *Ab ómnibus iniquitátibus meis érue me* → *Arrancai-me de todas as minhas iniquidades* (a source named, as 31:7); passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 38:9 *oppróbrium insipiénti dedísti me* → *fizestes de mim a afronta do insensato*** — draft 1 *uma afronta para o insensato*: the blind reader could not tell the direction; the stylist asked for a genitive (and *opróbrio*, refused per this row). The gate (minor) wanted the dative and *dar* back (*destes-me como afronta ao insensato*) — held: *afronta ao X* is heard as an insult offered to X. Option in Ps 38 `dedisti`.
Ps 38:12 *corripuísti hóminem* → *castigastes o homem*, as this row names.
Ps 38:12b *Et tabéscere fecísti sicut aráneam ánimam ejus* → *E fizestes a sua alma definhar como uma aranha* — unknown to the blind reader again; kept.

**Ps 38:13b *ádvena ego sum apud te, et peregrínus* → *eu sou forasteiro junto de vós, e peregrino*: ádvena here is πάροικος, the Greek behind íncola in 118:19, so by D15's test the two share *forasteiro* (this row said 'kept apart from ádvena' before the Greek was checked).** peregrínus (παρεπίδημος) → *peregrino* (MS1932; DRB 'sojourner'); 68:9 should follow. 93:6, 145:9 (ádvena, the stranger in the land) decide in their psalms. Passed the Latinist twice.

Ps 38:13 *Exáudi oratiónem meam, Dómine, et deprecatiónem meam* → *Escutai a minha oração, Senhor, e a minha prece* — this row's named place; the blind reader heard the two nouns as one thing said twice (the Latin's parallelism). The stylist's best line.
**Ps 38:13 *áuribus pércipe lácrimas meas* → *dai ouvidos às minhas lágrimas*** — a place this row named; D4 held; no reader remarked.

Ps 38:2 *ut non delínquam in lingua mea* → *para não cometer faltas com a minha língua* — the Greek is ἁμαρτάνειν here; the row held. The stylist found *cometer faltas* 'school register' and asked *pecar* (peccáre's; option in Ps 38 `delinquam`); the Latinist passed it twice.

Ps 38:7b the verb *Thesaurízat* → ***Acumula tesouros*** (*tesouros* = riches is the sense here): draft 1 *Entesoura* (MS1932) was unknown to the blind reader and left *os* (38:7b *cui congregábit ea* → *para quem os juntará*) without antecedent (Latinist, minor). The stylist's *Ajunta tesouros* refused: *ajunta … juntará* would make thesaurizáre and congregáre one verb.

Ps 38:7 *sed et frustra conturbátur* → *mas também em vão se perturba*; 38:12b *verúmtamen vane conturbátur omnis homo* → *todavia, em vão se perturba todo homem* (frustra and vane both μάτην → *em vão*).
Ps 38:10 *ámove a me plagas tuas* → *afastai de mim os vossos flagelos* (= 118:29's verb).

**Ps 38:10 *plagas tuas* → *os vossos flagelos*: plaga here is μάστιγας, the Greek of flagélla (31:10, 34:15), so D15 gives one word (MS1932, DRB 'scourges').** *flagelos* unknown to the blind reader again (heard punishments / plagues, which is the sense); *golpes* is option 2. plaga elsewhere (63:8 wounds, 72:4) decides locally.

**Ps 38:14 *Remítte mihi* (no object; Greek ἄνες μοι, 'let up') → *Perdoai-me*** (DRB 'O forgive me'; remíttere → perdoar as 31:1). The gate (minor) proposed *Relevai-me* (pardon and relieve at once) — held as option 2: *relevar alguém* is uncommon; the blind reader heard 'relent' second already.

Ps 38:6 *mensurábiles posuísti dies meos* → *pusestes em medida os meus dias* (MS1932; the Latin's verb kept): draft 1 *tornastes mensuráveis* — *mensuráveis* unknown to the blind reader, technical to the stylist; his *fizestes medidos* refused as this row's calque.
Ps 38:12 *ego deféci in increpatiónibus* → *eu desfaleci nas repreensões* (a person fainting — the right sense here, unlike 11:2). The stylist wanted *eu* dropped; kept for the Latin's *ego*.

terms: | substántia (a person's being: *substántia mea*) | o meu ser (*e o meu ser é como nada diante de vós*; *E o meu ser está junto de vós*) | open | Ps 38:6, 38:8 (ὑπόστασις both). *a minha substância* (DRB) is chemistry or philosophy in Portuguese; MS1932 *o meu ser* in 38:6 (*todos os meus bens* in 38:8 is property). Passed the Latinist twice; heard 'my being / existence'. **88:48 *quæ mea substántia* and 138:15 can follow; 108:11 (property → *bens*) and 68:3 *non est substántia* (footing) decide locally** (six lines, grep). |

| consístere (a person, *advérsum*) | erguer-se (*quando o pecador se erguia contra mim*) | open | Ps 38:2b (συστῆναι … ἐναντίον). Draft 1 *se postava* was unknown to the blind reader and stiff to the stylist; *erguer-se* is also one of astáre's words (D22) — they never meet in a verse. 26:3 (a camp) has *se instalar*. |
| obmutéscere | emudecer (*Emudeci*) | working | Ps 38:3, 38:10 — the only two places (grep); one word both times. |

| in imágine (38:7 *in imágine pertránsit homo*) | *como uma imagem* | open | ἐν εἰκόνι; DRB 'as an image', MS1932 *como uma sombra*. **The Latinist asked twice (minor) for *em imagem*, which keeps a reading 'in the image (of God)'** — held: not a Portuguese sentence. imágo also 72:20. |

| refrigeráre (passive) | ser reanimado (*para que eu seja reanimado antes de partir*) | open | Ps 38:14 (ἀναψύξω); draft 1 *tome alento* (MS1932): *alento* unknown to the blind reader, and the Latinist wanted the passive. Only verb place (grep); the noun refrigérium 65:12 and the refection row (22:2 *refrigério*). |

| esse absolute (*et ámplius non ero*) | existir (*e já não existirei*) | open | Ps 38:14; the bare *e não serei mais* hangs in Portuguese (and rhymed with 38:13b *pais*); the stylist's *e já não serei* is the option. |
